newsitem.title: BULGARIA: FEATURE-Bulgarian premier wins party confidence vote.
newsitem.headline: FEATURE-Bulgarian premier wins party confidence vote.

text.p: Bulgaria's Prime Minister Zhan Videnov on Tuesday won a confidence vote from his party by a narrow margin, giving him backing to stay in office and to seek introduction of an IMF-proposed currency board.

A total of 87 members of the party executive supported the premier, 69 voted against him and two abstained. The meeting made no cabinet changes and Videnov said any reshuffle would be discussed at a full party congress scheduled for December 21 and 22.
The plenum of the ruling Bulgarian Socialist Party met through the night to discuss calls for change after their defeat in November 3 presidential elections.
"The margin shows that support for the cabinet is inadequate and we have to work to increase it," Videnov said.
Three members of the executive board, including party vice chairman Yanaki Stoilov, resigned.

On Monday night, Videnov said he supported introduction of a currency board proposed by the International Monetary Fund (IMF) to restore confidence in the collapsing lev, and asked the party for backing to start negotiations.
